::: {.page-lede}
My teaching spans postgraduate and undergraduate courses in quantitative methods, statistics, research design, and sociology of education. I focus on helping students connect methodological choices to meaningful substantive questions.
:::

## Earlier teaching

Between 2017 and 2021, I supported undergraduate courses in psychological measurement, multivariate statistics, quantitative research strategies, descriptive and correlational statistics, and the social and political history of Chile and Latin America.

::: {.teaching-philosophy}
::: {.teaching-philosophy-copy}
<p class="eyebrow light">APPROACH</p>

## Methods are most useful when students can see the question behind them

I teach quantitative work as a sequence of research decisions: defining a question, understanding the data-generating process, choosing a defensible model, and communicating uncertainty with clarity.
:::

::: {.teaching-principles}
<div><strong>Concept first</strong><span>Build intuition before formalism.</span></div>
<div><strong>Applied practice</strong><span>Learn by working through real research problems.</span></div>
<div><strong>Transparent choices</strong><span>Make assumptions and trade-offs visible.</span></div>
:::
:::
